learn.hook: A banana peel can turn into soil in a few weeks, but a plastic bottle can stay around for hundreds of years. What happens to the things we throw away?
points: Pollution means making air, water or land dirty and harmful.
Smoke from vehicles, factories and burning garbage pollutes the air. Sewage and waste pollute water. Plastic and garbage pollute land.
Follow the 3 Rs: Reduce (use less), Reuse (use again) and Recycle (make new things from old ones).
Separate waste at home: wet waste like peels and leftover food goes in the green bin; dry waste like paper, plastic, metal and glass goes in the blue bin.
Wet kitchen waste can be turned into compost, a natural manure for plants. Carry a cloth bag instead of taking plastic bags.

example.q: After a birthday party, there are banana peels, paper plates, plastic spoons and a glass bottle. Think it through: how should they be sorted?
steps: Banana peels rot easily: they are wet waste for the green bin.
Paper plates, plastic spoons and the glass bottle are dry waste for the blue bin.
Even better next time: use steel plates and spoons that can be washed and reused.
example.answer: Peels in the green (wet) bin; paper, plastic and glass in the blue (dry) bin.

learn.reallife: Many cities, like Indore, collect wet and dry waste separately from every home. Does your colony's garbage van have two parts?

quiz.q: What does 'Reuse' mean?

Using something again instead of throwing it away
quiz.explain: Reusing, like using a jam jar as a pencil holder, means less waste.

quiz.q: Making new paper from old newspapers is an example of

quiz.q: Which of these causes air pollution?
quiz.explain: Burning garbage gives out smoke and harmful gases.

options: Natural manure made from rotting kitchen and garden waste
quiz.explain: Peels and leaves rot into dark, rich compost that helps plants grow.

quiz.q: Which is the best choice when you go shopping?
options: Ask for a new plastic bag every time
Carry a cloth bag from home
Throw the bag on the road after use

teach.nudge: What are the 3 Rs? And how should we separate our waste?

learn.hook: Have you heard grown-ups say 'summers are getting hotter'? Scientists have found that the Earth is slowly warming. What can we do about it?
points: Weather is what the sky and air are like today: sunny, rainy or windy. Climate is the usual weather of a place over many years.
Burning coal, petrol and diesel, and cutting down forests, add a lot of carbon dioxide to the air. This gas traps heat, so the Earth is slowly getting warmer.
A warmer Earth means melting glaciers, rising sea levels, more heatwaves, and very heavy rain or long dry spells in some places.
Trees take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen. Forests also give homes to animals and keep the soil in place.
We can help: plant and care for trees, save electricity, walk, cycle or use buses, and waste less.

example.q: Mumbai is warm and humid all year, while Shimla is cool most of the year. Is this weather or climate? Think it through.
steps: Weather changes from day to day.
Here we are talking about what a place is usually like over many years.
example.answer: It is climate: the usual weather of a place over many years.

learn.reallife: Many schools have eco-clubs that plant trees, save water and run 'no plastic' days. Each small step helps our shared home.

games.title: Weather or climate?
items: 'It is raining in Pune today' describes the weather.
Weather is about a particular day or time.
Climate is the usual weather of a place over many years.
Climate is the long-term pattern.
Cutting forests helps keep the Earth cool.
Trees take in carbon dioxide. Cutting them adds to warming.
Glaciers are melting faster because the Earth is getting warmer.

Trees give out oxygen.

quiz.q: What is climate?
options: The usual weather of a place over many years
quiz.explain: Climate is the long-term pattern of weather in a place.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up climate with weather

quiz.q: 'It is very foggy in Delhi this morning.' This tells us about the
quiz.explain: It describes one morning, so it is about the weather.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any weather talk is about climate

quiz.q: Which gas, added by burning fuels, traps heat and warms the Earth?
quiz.explain: Burning coal, petrol and diesel adds carbon dioxide, which traps heat.
quiz.mistake: Thinks oxygen causes warming

quiz.q: Which is a result of the Earth getting warmer?
quiz.explain: Higher temperatures make glaciers melt and sea levels rise.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the effects of warming

quiz.q: How do trees help fight the warming of the Earth?
options: They take in carbon dioxide from the air
quiz.explain: Trees use carbon dioxide to make their food, so they remove some of it from the air.
quiz.mistake: Does not know trees take in carbon dioxide

quiz.q: Which action helps protect our climate?
options: Leaving the AC on in an empty room
Switching off lights when not needed
quiz.explain: Saving electricity means less coal is burnt in power plants, so less carbon dioxide.
quiz.mistake: Does not link electricity use with burning fuels

quiz.q: A heatwave is
options: a big wave in the sea
a long spell of very hot weather
quiz.explain: A heatwave means many days of unusually hot weather. Drink water and stay in the shade.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'wave' means a sea wave

quiz.q: Which way of going to school puts the least smoke into the air?
options: Going alone in a big car
A car that waits with its engine running
quiz.explain: Walking and cycling burn no fuel at all.
quiz.mistake: Does not compare which travel uses fuel

teach.ask: Gappu fans himself with a leaf: 'Why is it getting so hot? Is it just today, or is the Earth changing?'
teach.praise: Oh! The Earth is warming because of the gases from burning fuels and cutting trees. Let's plant trees and save energy!
teach.nudge: Is this about one day's weather or the climate? And what is making the Earth warmer?

learn.hook: Ordinary people in India have hugged trees, grown whole forests and protected animals. You can be an Earth hero too!
points: In the Chipko movement, which began in 1973 in the hills of present-day Uttarakhand, villagers hugged trees to stop them from being cut. Gaura Devi and the women of Reni village were part of it.
The Bishnoi people of Rajasthan have protected trees and animals like blackbucks for hundreds of years. In 1730, Amrita Devi and many villagers bravely stood up to save khejri trees.
Jadav Payeng, the 'Forest Man of India', planted trees for years and grew a whole forest on a sandbar of the Brahmaputra in Assam.

National parks protect wildlife: Kaziranga (Assam) for the one-horned rhinoceros, Gir (Gujarat) for Asiatic lions, which live in the wild only in Gujarat, and Jim Corbett (Uttarakhand), India's first national park.
World Environment Day is on 5 June and Earth Day is on 22 April.

example.q: Your colony plans to cut a big old neem tree to make more parking space. Think it through: what could you do?
steps: The tree gives shade, oxygen and a home to birds.
Talk to your parents and the colony members about why the tree matters.
Suggest another place for parking, and plant more trees together.
example.answer: Speak up politely with adults, explain the tree's value and suggest other ideas.

learn.reallife: On World Environment Day, many schools plant saplings. If you plant one, give it a name and water it every week!

items.q: Movement in which people hugged trees

quiz.q: In the Chipko movement, people
options: hugged trees to stop them from being cut
quiz.explain: 'Chipko' means 'to cling' or 'to hug'. Villagers hugged trees to protect them.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what Chipko means

quiz.q: The Chipko movement began in the hills of which present-day state?
quiz.explain: It began in 1973 in the Garhwal hills, now part of Uttarakhand.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a state without knowing the history

quiz.q: Which community of Rajasthan is famous for protecting trees and blackbucks?
quiz.explain: The Bishnois have cared for khejri trees and animals like blackbucks for centuries.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up communities from different regions

quiz.q: Gir National Park in Gujarat is famous for the
quiz.explain: Asiatic lions live in the wild only in Gujarat, in and around Gir.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Gir with tiger or rhino parks

quiz.q: Kaziranga National Park in Assam is famous for the
quiz.explain: Kaziranga has the largest number of one-horned rhinos in the world.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up animals and their parks

quiz.q: Who is known as the 'Forest Man of India'?
quiz.explain: Jadav Payeng planted trees for many years and grew a forest on a sandbar of the Brahmaputra.
quiz.mistake: Mixes him up with other famous Indians

quiz.q: World Environment Day is celebrated on
quiz.explain: World Environment Day is on 5 June. 22 April is Earth Day and 22 March is World Water Day.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the different environment days

quiz.q: Which is India's first national park?
quiz.explain: Jim Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand was set up in 1936 and is India's first national park.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the most famous park must be the oldest

teach.ask: Gappu sits on a branch: 'Someone wants to cut my tree! Who are the people who protect trees and animals?'
teach.praise: Wow! Chipko huggers, the Bishnois and the Forest Man all protect nature. I'll be an Earth hero too!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me about people who saved trees? And where are animals protected?
